reason: The hypothesis relies on CALPHAD's ability to model mixing thermodynamics, but the cited evidence shows major gaps: E1 states that formation enthalpies of intermetallics are difficult to estimate and no general models exist, undermining the core premise; E3 notes that even with sufficient binary data, CALPHAD predictions of transformation temperatures are challenging; E4 demonstrates accuracy only for specific binary systems, not for the complex multi-component HEAs targeted. The premises are thus only partially supported.
premises: CALPHAD can compute Gibbs free energies for all competing phases in HEAs using mixing enthalpies and configurational entropies
Configurational entropy is easy to model and mixing enthalpy has been estimated for many atom pairs
CALPHAD predictions of phase types and numbers agree well with experiments when enough binary systems are assessed
Third-generation CALPHAD descriptions can accurately describe thermodynamic properties down to 0 K and near melting points
CALPHAD can be validated against DSC and thermal expansion measurements for melting properties
